solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Force rascal to perform

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone compels a young scoundrel to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the force of one body striking another, a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Garment thieves getting reported?

indicators.note: being reported means being spoken of, so the word for thieves is heard rather than read

parts.note: nickers are thieves, from British slang nick, to steal

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing gets thieves into the news.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for steal, so NICKERS are thieves; spoken, the word matches the underwear name.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are a British undergarment, an example of a garment.

clue.text: Our newspaper? Couples may sleep under it!

definitions.meaning: the Daily Telegraph is printed in the large-format style, so its own setter can call that format ours
read as two words, a ... is a wide bed sheet big enough for two sleepers

explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a large-format quality paper, and split up the word describes a wide bed linen.

clue.text: Specially produced, this local fabric

indicators.note: something specially produced is made up afresh, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A textile made specially in the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailcloth is the heavy canvas used for sails, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: State starts to undermine those admirable heroes

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A government sets out to undermine people who are rightly admired as heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, an example of a state.

clue.text: More primitive American dramatist

definitions.meaning: Thornton ... wrote the play Our Town

explanation.definitionFit: Wilder is the comparative of wild, meaning less tamed, and the surname of playwright Thornton Wilder.

clue.text: Lean Muse disturbed mythological king

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of place, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thin goddess of the arts is upset by a legendary monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Menelaus was the king of Sparta in Greek myth, husband of Helen.

clue.text: Ruler about to run into demonstration?

indicators.note: running into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A ruler is about to run into a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign, a ruler such as a king or queen.

clue.text: Hospital? That's awful, man!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, seen on road signs
ugh is an exclamation of disgust, saying something is awful

explanation.surface: Someone groans at the prospect of hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh is a man's first name, an example of a man.

clue.text: Sitting somehow in a street before journey

indicators.note: before places the street abbreviation ahead of the journey

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone sits awkwardly in a road before setting off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride describes a way of sitting with one leg on each side, so it is a manner of sitting.

clue.text: Port being wondrously divine

definitions.meaning: Arkhangelsk is a Russian port on the White Sea, also spelt this way in English
a chief angel, a heavenly being of great glory

explanation.definitionFit: The White Sea port shares its English name with a chief angel, a divine being.

clue.text: Horticulturalist's original border?

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener's first boundary planting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: the first letter of horticulturalist plus a border gives a living boundary a gardener plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of shrubs planted as a boundary, a gardener's living border.

clue.text: Elders perhaps giving time to returning prophet

indicators.note: returning means the word for the prophet comes back, read from the end

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: Senior citizens spend time with a prophet who has come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elders' suggests older people; here it is the elder tree. 'returning' turns SEER into REES.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a kind of shrub or small tree, so elders are examples of trees.

clue.text: The French certificate presented to a group of stars

parts.note: la is a French word for the
cert is short for certificate

explanation.surface: A French document is handed to a band of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerta, the Lizard, is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Woman at home with man in one American state or another

parts.note: Carol is a woman's name
in means at home
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A woman stays home with a man in some American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carolinian comes from North or South Carolina, so the word fits either of two states.

clue.text: Justify giving nit advice that's wrong

indicators.note: advice that is wrong is out of order, so its letters with nit are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone defends handing out mistaken guidance about head lice.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate is to show to be right, a verb synonym of justify.

clue.text: Revised test sent out — groups hoping to gain advantage?

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: An updated exam is posted to candidates angling for an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'Revised' looks like one but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Vested interests are parties standing to profit from something, groups out for their own gain.

clue.text: Woman wanting business centre to present the truth

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A woman going without a commercial district has to tell the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, the quality of being truthful, a near synonym.

clue.text: Team fixes first mechanical device

indicators.note: first places the word for fixes ahead of the team

parts.note: sets means fixes, as in sets a date
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A squad sorts out the opening problem with machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew is a screw that holds a part in place, a small mechanical device.

clue.text: Well-respected film director's outside place

indicators.note: outside means the director's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Carol Reed was a British film director, of The Third Man
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A movie director's location is outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol Reed directed The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means held in good repute, well regarded.

clue.text: Time when there's rising anger in school

indicators.note: in means the reversed anger goes inside the school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upward, so the word for anger is turned round

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A moment of mounting fury in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IRE into ERI; 'school' is a pod of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A period is a stretch of time, a noun synonym.

clue.text: University learner bowled over by fashion in town

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked upside down, so these two letters are turned round

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates
ton is an old word for fashion, as in high style

explanation.surface: A student at a university is overwhelmed by style in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London. 'bowled over' makes LU from U and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire in England, an example of a town.

clue.text: Relations creating awful scene around one

indicators.note: around means the jumbled word is placed round the single letter
something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Family members cause a terrible fuss around someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges SCENE as NECES, which goes 'around' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nieces are daughters of one's siblings, examples of relations.

clue.text: Indian in narrow inlet not completely visible

indicators.note: not all of the word can be seen, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a creek is a narrow inlet

explanation.surface: A Native American in a narrow inlet is partly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people, so a Cree is an American Indian.

clue.text: Tree from which swan crosses a river

indicators.note: crosses means stretches across, so the swan goes round the other letters

parts.note: a cob is a male swan

explanation.surface: A tree from which a swan flies across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean tree whose pods taste like chocolate.

clue.text: US President following British vehicle

indicators.note: following places the president's name after the British letter

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: An American president tags along behind a British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A bike is a bicycle or motorbike, an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Written account, very bad article in French

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A terrible French article as a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written record of events in order, a written account.

clue.text: Stole the thing outside back of mill, set of implements

indicators.note: outside means those words go around the letter from the mill

parts.note: stole means took

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: it means the thing

explanation.surface: Someone took the item from behind the factory, a collection of tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolkit is a set of tools, the implements for a job.

clue.text: Piece of furniture in entrance to the west before

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture stands in a doorway facing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' turns GATE into ETAG.
explanation.definitionFit: An etagere is a stand of open shelves, a piece of furniture.
